intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the iconic 14th-century Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok robe. Many rental shops surrounding the palace offer affordable Hanbok rentals, and wearing one grants you free entry to the palace. Witness the ceremonial Changing of the Royal Guard and stroll through the grand courtyards for an immersive dive into Joseon Dynasty culture.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional market, famous for its vibrant food stalls. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (mini seaweed rice rolls), tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the authentic sights, sounds, and flavors of everyday Korean culinary life.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Dance Class
experiences.description: Learn choreography from your favorite K-Pop songs at one of Hongdae's many dedicated K-Pop dance academies. Professional instructors teach routines from groups like BTS, BLACKPINK, and NewJeans in a fun, energetic group setting. This is a quintessential K-culture experience that lets you live out your idol fantasies and connect with fellow K-Pop fans from around the world.

experiences.name: Insadong Cultural Village & Tea House Exploration
experiences.description: Wander through the charming alleyways of Insadong, Seoul's premier cultural district filled with traditional tea houses, antique shops, indie galleries, and Korean craft stores. Stop into a traditional Hanok-style tea house to enjoy a ceremonial cup of omija (five-flavor berry) or barley tea paired with Korean rice cakes. Explore Ssamziegil, a quirky open-air shopping complex showcasing local artisan goods and handmade crafts.

experiences.name: Authentic Korean BBQ Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Enjoy a classic Korean BBQ dinner at one of Mapo-gu's legendary charcoal grill restaurants, famous for their premium samgyeopsal (pork belly) and galbi (beef short ribs). Grill your own meat tableside, wrap it in fresh perilla leaves and lettuce, and pair it with an array of banchan (side dishes) and a glass of soju or makgeolli. This communal dining ritual is central to Korean social culture and an unmissable culinary highlight.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or limousine bus to Bupyeong station. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store for easy transit use throughout the trip.

meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at a 24-hour GS25 or CU convenience store near the hotel — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or a hot dog (under ₩5,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — just check in and rest. Exchange some cash at the airport (Incheon has competitive rates). A T-money card costs ₩2,500 and can be loaded at any subway station or convenience store. Bupyeong is well-connected to Seoul via subway Line 1 and Line 7.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a walk through Bupyeong Modoo Mall underground shopping street — one of Korea's largest underground markets. Browse affordable K-fashion, accessories, and street snacks. Get oriented with the local neighborhood around the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take subway Line 1 to Seoul Station, then transfer to Gyeongbokgung Palace (Line 3, Gyeongbokgung Station). Explore the grand Joseon-era palace grounds, including Geunjeongjeon Hall and the scenic Hyangwonjeong Pavilion. Rent a hanbok at one of the nearby rental shops (₩10,000–₩15,000/hour) for free palace entry and great photos.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Insadong, Seoul's cultural arts district. Stroll the main street lined with traditional tea houses, craft shops, and street food stalls. Visit Ssamziegil courtyard for indie shops and K-culture vibes.

meals.breakfast: Toyoko Inn complimentary breakfast or a convenience store meal (₩3,000–₩5,000)
meals.lunch: Gyeongbokgung area — try Tosokchon Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup, ₩17,000) or a cheaper bibimbap set at a nearby local restaurant (₩8,000–₩10,000)
meals.dinner: Insadong street food — hotteok (sweet pancake), tteokbokki, and odeng (fish cake skewers) for under ₩10,000 total

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. Since today is Wednesday, it's open. Dress warmly — temperatures around 3°C. The palace grounds are beautiful in winter with minimal crowds. Hanbok rental shops are clustered near the palace's main gate.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Bukchon Hanok Village (take Line 3 to Anguk Station). Walk through the preserved traditional Korean hanok alleyways with stunning views of the city. This is one of Seoul's most photogenic neighborhoods and completely free to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill to Changdeokgung Palace and the Secret Garden (Huwon). Book a guided tour of the Secret Garden in advance (₩8,000). The winter scenery of bare trees and traditional architecture is hauntingly beautiful. Afterward, explore Changdeokgung's main palace grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) area. The futuristic Zaha Hadid-designed building is free to walk around and beautifully lit at night. Browse the nearby Dongdaemun Market for affordable clothing and accessories.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a bakery near Bupyeong station (Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours, ₩3,000–₩6,000)
meals.lunch: Anguk area — try a traditional Korean set meal (한정식 hanjeongshik lite) at a local restaurant (₩10,000–₩12,000) or a simple dosirak (lunchbox) from a nearby shop
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area pojangmacha (street food tent) — grilled skewers, tteokbokki, and soju for ₩10,000–₩15,000

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours are limited and must be booked online at the Cultural Heritage Administration website. Book at least a day ahead. Bukchon Hanok Village has noise restrictions — be respectful of residents. Wear non-slip shoes as the alleyways can be icy in December.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namdaemun Market (Line 4, Hoehyeon Station) — one of Korea's oldest and largest traditional markets. Explore stalls selling everything from clothing to kitchenware. Try the famous Namdaemun kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) alley for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Myeongdong, Seoul's famous shopping and K-beauty district. Browse affordable skincare at Innisfree, The Face Shop, and Etude House. Sample street food along the main pedestrian street. Visit Myeongdong Cathedral, a stunning Gothic landmark that's free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Take the cable car up to N Seoul Tower on Namsan Mountain (cable car ₩9,500 round trip, tower observation deck ₩21,000 — skip the deck and enjoy the free outdoor plaza and city views). The tower is beautifully lit at night and the love locks are iconic K-culture.

meals.breakfast: Namdaemun Market — kalguksu noodle soup (₩7,000) or hotteok from a street stall (₩1,500)
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food lunch — try a corn dog, tteokbokki, and a cup of tanghuru (candied fruit skewer) for under ₩10,000
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja restaurant (famous for kalguksu and mandu dumplings, ₩9,000–₩12,000) — expect a queue but it moves fast

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong street food vendors are most active in the afternoon and evening. Many K-beauty shops offer free samples — great for trying products without spending. The Namsan cable car can have queues on weekends; consider hiking up the trail instead (free, about 30 minutes) for a budget option.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Hongdae (Line 2, Hongik University Station) — Seoul's youth culture and indie music hub. Explore the vibrant street art, murals, and quirky shops in the surrounding alleys. Visit the free Hongdae street performance area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area. The campus is architecturally stunning and free to walk through. Browse the affordable shopping streets around Sinchon for K-fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the evening atmosphere. Saturday nights in Hongdae are electric — street buskers perform K-pop covers and original music. Visit a norebang (karaoke room) for a quintessential K-culture experience (₩10,000–₩15,000/hour per room, split among friends).

meals.lunch: Hongdae area — try a Korean fried chicken and beer (chimaek) combo at a local restaurant (₩15,000–₩18,000) or a cheaper ramyeon shop (₩5,000–₩7,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae street food or a budget Korean BBQ spot — many restaurants near Hongdae offer affordable samgyeopsal (pork belly) sets for ₩10,000–₩13,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Saturdays in Hongdae are very lively but also crowded. The area is famous for its indie music scene and K-pop culture. Many free street performances happen near the main park area. Norebang is a must-do K-culture experience — look for 'coin norebang' (코인노래방) for the cheapest option at ₩500–₩1,000 per song.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gwangjang Market (Line 1 or 2, Jongno 5-ga Station) — one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. This is a food lover's paradise. Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), and yukhoe (beef tartare) for breakfast/brunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along Cheonggyecheon Stream — a beautifully restored urban stream running through central Seoul. The 5.8km stream walk is free and peaceful. In December, it may feature winter light festival decorations. End at the청계광장 (Cheonggye Plaza) near City Hall.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Seoul City Hall Plaza and Deoksugung Palace. The palace is beautifully lit at night and the changing of the royal guard ceremony is a highlight (check schedule). Walk through the nearby Jeong-dong area with its historic buildings.

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market — mayak kimbap (₩3,000) and bindaetteok (₩4,000) — budget feast under ₩10,000
meals.lunch: Cheonggyecheon area — find a local 백반 (baekban) restaurant for a full Korean meal with rice, soup, and multiple side dishes for ₩7,000–₩9,000
meals.dinner: Deoksugung area or City Hall — try a sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) restaurant for a warming winter meal (₩8,000–₩10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is one of the most authentic food market experiences in Seoul — made famous internationally by Netflix's Street Food series. Go hungry! The Deoksugung Palace night admission is available on select days — check the schedule at the Cultural Heritage Administration website. The Cheonggyecheon Stream walk is flat and easy but can be cold — dress in layers.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bukhansan National Park (take Line 3 to Gupabal Station, then bus). Hike one of the accessible trails — the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail is manageable in winter and offers stunning views of Seoul surrounded by mountains. The park entrance is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the hike or explore the fortress walls. The ancient stone fortress walls date back to the Joseon Dynasty. Return to the city by mid-afternoon. Stop at a local restaurant near the park entrance for a post-hike meal.
day_by_day.evening: Rest evening back in Bupyeong. Explore the local Bupyeong area — visit the underground Modoo Mall for some shopping, or relax at a local jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) for a budget wellness experience (₩10,000–₩15,000).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — pack snacks for the hike
meals.lunch: Pack kimbap from a convenience store (₩1,500–₩2,500) or eat at a mountain trail restaurant near the park (doenjang jjigae set, ₩8,000–₩10,000)
meals.dinner: Local Bupyeong restaurant — try a Korean army stew (budae jjigae) which originated near Incheon, ₩10,000–₩13,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Winter hiking requires proper footwear — trails can be icy. Bring microspike attachments if possible (available at outdoor shops near the trailhead). The park is less crowded on weekdays. A jjimjilbang visit is a quintessential Korean experience — you can sleep there overnight if needed for extra budget savings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea (Line 4 or 6, Samgakji Station) — one of Seoul's most impressive and completely free museums. The outdoor exhibits include tanks, aircraft, and warships. The indoor galleries cover Korean history from ancient times through the Korean War.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Itaewon (Line 6, Itaewon Station) — Seoul's most international neighborhood. Explore the diverse shops, vintage clothing stores, and multicultural atmosphere. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art exterior (free to view) or browse the antique shops on Antique Furniture Street.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Haebangchon (HBC) — a hillside neighborhood adjacent to Itaewon with a bohemian, artsy vibe. The area has affordable international restaurants and cozy bars. Great for experiencing Seoul's expat and creative community culture.

meals.lunch: War Memorial area — find a local 식당 (sikdang) for a budget Korean lunch set (₩7,000–₩9,000)
meals.dinner: Haebangchon — try a local Korean restaurant or one of the affordable international options (many offer meals under ₩12,000)

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial of Korea is closed on Mondays — since today is Tuesday, it's open. This is one of Seoul's best free attractions and shouldn't be missed. Itaewon has a very different vibe from other Seoul neighborhoods — it's more international and diverse. Haebangchon is a 10-minute walk uphill from Itaewon station.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World (Line 2 or 8, Jamsil Station) — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks. Budget option: skip the rides and just explore the free outdoor Magic Island area and the adjacent Seokchon Lake, which is beautifully decorated for the Christmas season. Walk around the lake for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jamsil area — visit the free Lotte World Mall (one of Korea's largest shopping malls) for window shopping and food court dining. Walk to Olympic Park (Line 5, Olympic Park Station) — a massive free park with outdoor sculptures and winter scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam (Line 2, Gangnam Station) for the evening. Walk the famous Gangnam-daero boulevard made famous by PSY's 'Gangnam Style.' Browse the underground COEX Mall and visit the free Starfield Library inside COEX — a stunning Instagram-worthy library.

meals.lunch: Lotte World Mall food court — wide variety of Korean and international options for ₩8,000–₩12,000
meals.dinner: Gangnam area — try a local Korean restaurant away from the main tourist strip for better prices (dosirak or bibimbap sets ₩8,000–₩10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Lotte World admission is expensive (₩62,000+) — skip the park itself and enjoy the free outdoor areas and lake. The Seokchon Lake Christmas decorations are spectacular and free to enjoy. The Starfield Library in COEX is free and one of Seoul's most photogenic spots. Gangnam is pricier than other areas — eat at local restaurants one block off the main street.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (Line 3, Anguk Station) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in Seoul. The temple is free to enter and beautifully decorated with lanterns. In December, it may have special winter decorations. Explore the surrounding Insadong area for traditional crafts and tea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ihwa Mural Village on Naksan Mountain — a charming hillside neighborhood covered in colorful murals and street art. The famous 'Moon Cat' mural is a must-see. The area is free to explore and offers great views of Seoul. Walk the Naksan Park trail along the old city wall.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration! Head to Myeongdong or Hongdae for the festive atmosphere. Streets are decorated, carolers perform, and the city feels magical. Join the crowds for street food and the holiday atmosphere. Many young Koreans celebrate Christmas Eve as a romantic holiday.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or a traditional Korean breakfast at a local restaurant near Bupyeong (해장국 haejangguk, hangover soup, ₩8,000)
meals.lunch: Insadong area — try a traditional Korean tea house for yuja tea and rice cakes (₩5,000–₩8,000) or a nearby restaurant
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve street food in Myeongdong or Hongdae — budget ₩15,000–₩20,000 for a festive street food spread

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the busiest nights in Seoul — expect large crowds in Myeongdong, Hongdae, and Gangnam. Book any restaurant reservations well in advance. The festive atmosphere is incredible and very K-culture — Christmas in Korea is celebrated more as a couples' holiday than a family one. Jogyesa Temple is a peaceful contrast to the commercial Christmas atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (Line 5, Seodaemun Station) — a lesser-visited but beautiful palace that's free to enter. The grounds are peaceful and uncrowded. Nearby is the Seoul Museum of History, which is also free and provides excellent context for understanding Seoul's development.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Seochon Village area near Gyeongbokgung — a charming neighborhood of traditional hanok houses converted into cafes, galleries, and boutiques. This is where many Korean artists and intellectuals have historically lived. Browse the independent shops and cozy cafes.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a Korean jjimjilbang (sauna/bathhouse) for a relaxing Christmas evening — a very Korean way to spend the holiday. Many families visit jjimjilbangs on holidays. Enjoy the various hot rooms, cold pools, and communal areas. Some jjimjilbangs have restaurants inside.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — treat yourself on Christmas morning
meals.lunch: Seochon Village cafe — many offer affordable brunch sets or light meals (₩8,000–₩12,000)
meals.dinner: Jjimjilbang restaurant or a nearby local Korean restaurant — try samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) for a warming Christmas dinner (₩15,000–₩18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Korea is a public holiday — most government sites and some businesses may be closed or have reduced hours. Jjimjilbangs are typically open 24/7 and are very popular on holidays. The Seochon Village area is one of Seoul's best-kept secrets — less touristy than Bukchon but equally charming.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Folk Museum of Korea (inside Gyeongbokgung Palace grounds, free with palace admission or free on its own). Excellent exhibits on traditional Korean life, customs, and culture. Great for deepening K-culture knowledge before the trip ends.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Mangwon Market (Line 6, Mangwon Station) — a local neighborhood market beloved by Seoul residents and less touristy than Gwangjang. Browse fresh produce, street food, and local goods. Walk along the nearby Hangang River at Mangwon Hangang Park — beautiful winter views.
day_by_day.evening: Final big night out in Hongdae — do some last-minute souvenir shopping at the affordable shops and markets. Visit a coin norebang for a fun farewell K-culture experience. Enjoy the vibrant Saturday night atmosphere one last time.

meals.lunch: Mangwon Market street food — try the famous egg bread (계란빵 gyeran-ppang, ₩1,500), tteokbokki, and sundae (Korean blood sausage) for under ₩10,000
meals.dinner: Hongdae — splurge slightly on a proper Korean BBQ dinner for the last night (samgyeopsal or galbi, ₩15,000–₩20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mangwon Market is a great alternative to the more famous markets — very local and authentic. The Hangang River in winter is cold but beautiful, especially at sunset. For souvenirs, Hongdae and Insadong offer the best value — avoid airport shops which are significantly more expensive. Pack any liquid skincare products in checked luggage.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out of Toyoko Inn (store luggage at the hotel if possible). Take a final walk through Bupyeong Modoo Mall for any last-minute shopping. Pick up Korean snacks, instant ramen, and convenience store items to bring home as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time: if afternoon/evening flight, head to Incheon Airport via AREX from Seoul Station or direct bus from Bupyeong. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute gifts (cosmetics and Korean snacks are good value).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Enjoy a final Korean meal at the airport food court (try a bowl of bibimbap or doenjang jjigae for ₩10,000–₩13,000 before clearing security).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a final convenience store meal — stock up on Korean snacks for the flight
meals.lunch: Bupyeong area or airport — final Korean meal before departure
meals.dinner: Airport food court or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Check your specific flight departure time and plan accordingly — this itinerary assumes a late afternoon or evening departure. The AREX (Airport Railroad Express) from Seoul Station to Incheon Airport takes about 43 minutes (₩9,500) or the all-stop train takes about 66 minutes (₩4,950). From Bupyeong, take Line 1 to Seoul Station for the AREX. Allow extra time for check-in and security on busy travel days. Keep your T-money card — it can be refunded at the airport.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage. Take Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or limousine bus to Bupyeong area. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Grab a late-night snack near the hotel at a nearby convenience store (GS25 or CU) or a 24-hour pojangmacha (street food tent).

meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store snacks or instant ramen — try CU or GS25 near the hotel for Korean-style cup noodles, triangle kimbap, and hotteok (₩3,000–₩8,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you'll be tired from the flight. Prepare your T-money card at the airport for easy transit use throughout the trip. Dress warmly; December temperatures average around 3°C. The hotel is in Bupyeong-gu, Incheon, well connected by subway Line 1 to Seoul.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. Enjoy the hotel's complimentary breakfast (Toyoko Inn typically offers a simple Japanese-style breakfast). Afterward, explore the Bupyeong area — visit Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center (부평지하상가), one of Korea's largest underground malls, great for affordable K-fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take subway Line 1 to Incheon's Chinatown and Sinpo International Market area (~20 min). Explore Incheon Chinatown, Korea's only official Chinatown, with colorful murals and unique Jajangmyeon (black bean noodle) culture. Walk up to Jayu Park (Freedom Park) for a panoramic view of Incheon Port. Visit the nearby Open Port area with its historic Japanese and Western colonial architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Bupyeong for dinner. Explore Bupyeong Modoo Mall area for evening street food. Try the local night market vibe around Bupyeong Station exits.

meals.breakfast: Toyoko Inn complimentary breakfast (Japanese-style rice, miso soup, toast)
meals.lunch: Incheon Chinatown — try authentic Jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) or Jjamppong (spicy seafood noodles) at a local Chinese-Korean restaurant like Gonghwachun (₩10,000–₩15,000)
meals.dinner: Sinpo Dakgangjeong (신포닭강정) — famous sweet and spicy fried chicken near Sinpo Market, or grilled pork belly (samgyeopsal) at a local Bupyeong BBQ restaurant (₩15,000–₩25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is an orientation day — stay close to the hotel and Incheon to ease into the trip. Incheon has its own rich history and culture worth exploring before heading to Seoul. Wear layers and a warm coat.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 1 from Bupyeong to Seoul Station (~50 min, ₩1,500 with T-money). Head to Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁), the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Arrive early (~9:00 AM) to beat crowds. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) from a nearby rental shop for free palace entry and beautiful winter photos against the palace backdrop (₩15,000–₩25,000 for 2 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌한옥마을), a preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses with stunning views of the city. Explore the narrow alleyways and small galleries. Continue to Insadong (인사동) — Seoul's cultural arts district — browse traditional crafts, pottery, calligraphy shops, and unique K-culture souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Insadong for dinner and evening exploration. Visit Ssamziegil (쌈지길), a quirky open-air shopping complex with indie shops and cafes. Enjoy the festive winter atmosphere with holiday lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a pastry and coffee at a Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours near Bupyeong Station (₩5,000–₩8,000)
meals.lunch: Insadong traditional Korean set meal (한정식 스타일) at a local restaurant — try Sanchon or a similar spot for a cultural dining experience (₩15,000–₩20,000)
meals.dinner: Insadong area — try Dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) or Bibimbap at a cozy local restaurant (₩10,000–₩15,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. December lighting at the palace is magical. Hanbok rental is highly recommended for photos. Bring hand warmers — it will be cold standing outside. Return to hotel via subway Line 1 from Jonggak or Gyeongbokgung Station.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower / 남산서울타워) via cable car from Myeongdong. Enjoy panoramic winter views of Seoul from the observation deck (₩21,000 for observatory entry). See the famous love locks on the fence. The tower is especially beautiful on clear winter mornings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Myeongdong (명동) — Seoul's most famous shopping and street food district. Browse cosmetics shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), fashion stores, and international brands. Spend the afternoon sampling Myeongdong's legendary street food stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Explore명동 evening atmosphere — the area is lively with holiday decorations in December. Visit명동 Cathedral (Myeongdong Cathedral), a stunning Gothic Catholic church beautifully lit at night. Head back to hotel via subway.

meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food feast — try egg bread (계란빵), tornado potato, tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), hotteok, and Korean corn dogs (₩10,000–₩15,000 total for multiple snacks)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja (명동교자) — famous for handmade kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and mandu (dumplings), a Seoul institution (₩10,000–₩14,000)

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong is extremely popular with tourists but is a must-visit for K-beauty shopping. Olive Young is the best one-stop shop for Korean skincare and cosmetics at mid-range prices. Friday evenings can be crowded — go early for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (비원/후원). The Secret Garden tour requires advance booking (₩8,000 for palace + ₩5,000 for garden). The winter landscape of bare trees and frozen ponds is hauntingly beautiful. Explore the adjacent Changgyeonggung Palace as well.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP / 동대문디자인플라자) — a futuristic landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. Explore the design exhibitions and the surrounding Dongdaemun fashion district. Browse the massive fabric and fashion wholesale markets nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Dongdaemun is famous for its late-night shopping culture. The markets come alive after dark. Explore Doota Mall and Migliore for K-fashion. The area is vibrant on Saturday nights.

meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village (익선동) nearby — a trendy neighborhood with fusion Korean cafes and restaurants in restored hanok buildings. Try a modern Korean lunch set (₩12,000–₩18,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area — try Pyeongyang Naengmyeon (평양냉면, cold buckwheat noodles) at Woo Lae Oak or similar, or hearty Seolleongtang (ox bone soup) at a local restaurant (₩12,000–₩16,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Secret Garden tour in advance at the official Changdeokgung website. Saturday is busy — arrive at the palace early. Dongdaemun markets are open until 5 AM, so no rush in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hongdae (홍대) — Seoul's vibrant university district known for indie music, street art, and youth culture. Visit the Hongdae Free Market (if operating in winter, usually weekends). Browse the quirky shops, K-pop merchandise stores, and street art murals. Experience the creative energy of this neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area for more shopping and cafe culture. Then head to Yeouido Hangang Park (여의도한강공원) for a winter riverside walk. The Han River in winter is serene and beautiful. Rent a bike or simply stroll along the riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the famous Sunday evening busking performances near Hongdae Station Exit 9. Live music, dance performances, and street art make for an authentic K-culture experience. Explore the nightlife district.

meals.breakfast: Hongdae area brunch — try a trendy Korean brunch cafe like Cafe Bora or a local brunch spot (₩10,000–₩15,000)
meals.lunch: Sinchon area — try Budae Jjigae (부대찌개, Army Stew) — a Korean-American fusion stew born near US military bases, hearty and perfect for cold weather (₩12,000–₩15,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Hongdae — Korean BBQ at a mid-range restaurant, try Samgyeopsal (pork belly) or Chadolbaegi (beef brisket) with soju (₩20,000–₩30,000 per person including drinks)

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is best experienced in the afternoon and evening when the energy peaks. Sunday busking is a highlight of Seoul's street culture. The area has excellent K-pop merchandise shops if that's of interest.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour from Seoul by subway (Line 1 from Bupyeong to Suwon, ~1 hour). Walk the 5.7 km fortress walls surrounding the old city. The fortress is stunning in winter with minimal crowds. Visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace inside the fortress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's traditional market area near the fortress. Visit Paldalmun Gate and the surrounding traditional market streets. Suwon is also famous for its galbi (grilled short ribs) — a must-try local specialty.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong/Incheon area. Relax at the hotel or explore a local jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) near Bupyeong for a traditional Korean wellness experience (₩10,000–₩15,000 entry).

meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (수원갈비) — Suwon is the birthplace of this style of grilled beef short ribs. Try it at a local restaurant near the fortress (₩20,000–₩30,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Local Bupyeong restaurant — try Doenjang Jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew) with rice and banchan (side dishes) at a homestyle Korean restaurant (₩8,000–₩12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is one of Korea's best-preserved historical sites and often overlooked by tourists. The fortress walk takes 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace. Wear very warm shoes as the fortress walls are exposed to wind. Monday is a good day to visit as weekend crowds are gone.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Gangnam (강남) district — Seoul's upscale southern district. Visit COEX Mall, one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls, and the famous COEX Starfield Library (별마당 도서관) — a stunning open library with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, free to enter and perfect for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Apgujeong Rodeo Street (압구정 로데오) and Garosu-gil (가로수길) — tree-lined streets with boutique shops, concept stores, and trendy cafes. This is the heart of Seoul's luxury and K-fashion scene. Visit the SM Entertainment building area (K-pop culture hub) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Bongeunsa Temple (봉은사) — a 1,200-year-old Buddhist temple dramatically situated next to the modern COEX complex. The temple is beautifully lit in the evening and offers a peaceful contrast to the surrounding urban landscape. Free entry.

meals.lunch: COEX food court or a restaurant in Gangnam — try Korean-style Chinese food (Jjajangmyeon and Tangsuyuk) or a modern Korean lunch set (₩12,000–₩18,000)
meals.dinner: Garosu-gil area — try a trendy Korean fusion restaurant or a classic Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) restaurant for a warming winter meal (₩15,000–₩20,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gangnam is a stark contrast to the traditional areas visited earlier — it showcases modern, affluent Seoul. COEX Starfield Library is free and one of Seoul's most Instagrammable spots. Bongeunsa Temple hosts templestay programs if interested in a deeper cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park (북한산국립공원) for a winter mountain hike. Take subway to Gupabal Station and hike the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail — a moderate hike with stunning views of Seoul from ancient fortress walls. The snow-dusted peaks in December are spectacular. Allow 3–4 hours for the hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and head to Seochon Village (서촌마을) — a charming, less-touristy neighborhood near Gyeongbokgung with traditional hanok houses converted into indie cafes, art galleries, and bookshops. More authentic and local than Bukchon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Gwanghwamun Square (광화문광장) — Seoul's grand central plaza with the iconic statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin. The square is beautifully decorated for the winter holiday season. Visit the nearby Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) for a romantic evening walk along the illuminated waterway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eat well before the hike
meals.lunch: Pack a convenience store lunch for the hike, or eat at a mountain trail restaurant (산장) near the park entrance — try Doenjang Jjigae or Bibimbap (₩8,000–₩12,000)
meals.dinner: Seochon or Gwanghwamun area — try Haemul Pajeon (해물파전, seafood scallion pancake) and Makgeolli (Korean rice wine) at a traditional pojangmacha or local restaurant (₩15,000–₩20,000)

day_by_day.notes: Check weather before hiking — icy conditions on mountain trails require hiking boots with good grip. Bring crampons or microspikes if available. The hike is rewarding but requires physical fitness. Cheonggyecheon Stream is a 5.8 km urban stream — walk as much or as little as you like.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) in Yongsan — a powerful and comprehensive museum covering Korean military history from ancient times through the Korean War. Free entry to the outdoor exhibits; indoor museum is ₩5,000. Sobering and deeply educational.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Itaewon (이태원) — Seoul's most international neighborhood, known for diverse food, multicultural atmosphere, and unique shopping. Browse the antique shops on Antique Furniture Street and explore the neighborhood's eclectic character. Visit Haebangchon (HBC) — a hip neighborhood on the hillside above Itaewon with great cafes and street art.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration! Head to Myeongdong Cathedral for the Christmas Eve Mass (a beautiful cultural experience even for non-Christians). The cathedral and surrounding streets are magnificently decorated. Afterward, join the festive crowds in Myeongdong for holiday shopping and street food.

meals.lunch: Itaewon — explore the diverse international food scene. Try a Korean-Mexican fusion burrito, Middle Eastern food, or authentic Indian curry (₩12,000–₩18,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — treat yourself to a nice Korean BBQ dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Myeongdong or Itaewon. Try Chadolbaegi (beef brisket) or Galbi (short ribs) with all the banchan (₩25,000–₩35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of Seoul's biggest celebration nights — the city is beautifully decorated and very lively. Myeongdong Cathedral's midnight mass is a unique cultural experience. Book dinner reservations in advance as restaurants fill up quickly on Christmas Eve.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World (롯데월드) — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks, located in Jamsil. Christmas Day is a magical time to visit with special decorations and performances. Enjoy the indoor theme park rides, ice skating rink, and folk museum (₩59,000 for day pass).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Lotte World or head to the adjacent Lotte World Tower — the 5th tallest building in the world. Visit the Seoul Sky Observatory on floors 117–123 for breathtaking 360° views of Seoul (₩27,000). The view on a clear winter day is extraordinary.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Jamsil and Seokchon Lake (석촌호수) — a beautiful lake next to Lotte World, decorated with Christmas lights and holiday installations. The lake walk is free and magical in the evening. Nearby Songpa-gu has excellent local restaurants.

meals.lunch: Lotte World food court or restaurants inside the complex — try Korean fried chicken and beer (치맥) or a Korean set meal (₩12,000–₩18,000)
meals.dinner: Jamsil area — try Jokbal (족발, braised pig's trotters) — a Korean Christmas tradition for many locals, or Bossam (보쌈, boiled pork wraps) at a local restaurant (₩15,000–₩25,000)

day_by_day.notes: Lotte World is very popular on Christmas Day — arrive early to avoid long queues. The Seoul Sky Observatory requires a separate ticket from Lotte World. Seokchon Lake's Christmas light festival (if running) is one of Seoul's most beautiful seasonal events.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namdaemun Market (남대문시장) — Seoul's largest traditional market, open since 1414. Explore the labyrinthine stalls selling everything from clothing and accessories to kitchenware and food. A true immersion into everyday Korean commerce and culture. Arrive early for the best experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Han River (한강) Banpo Bridge area. Visit Banpo Hangang Park and see the Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain (분수쇼) — note it may not operate in winter, but the riverside park is still beautiful. Walk across the bridge for city views. Then explore the trendy Banpo/Seorae Village (서래마을) — Seoul's French village neighborhood with charming cafes.
day_by_day.evening: Final major evening in Seoul — head to Dongdaemun for a last shopping spree. Visit the night markets and pick up any remaining souvenirs. Alternatively, enjoy a final Korean BBQ dinner with new friends or fellow travelers.

meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market — try Galchi Jorim (갈치조림, braised hairtail fish) or Kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) at one of the market's famous food stalls (₩8,000–₩12,000)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a nice Korean restaurant. Try Hanwoo (한우, Korean beef) BBQ or a traditional Korean multi-course meal (₩30,000–₩50,000 per person) to celebrate the trip

day_by_day.notes: Namdaemun Market is great for last-minute souvenir shopping — Korean snacks, ginseng products, dried seafood, and traditional crafts make excellent gifts. Saturday markets are lively but crowded. Start packing tonight as tomorrow is the last full day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — visit a local jjimjilbang (찜질방, Korean sauna) near Bupyeong for a relaxing traditional Korean spa experience to end the trip on a wellness note (₩10,000–₩15,000). Enjoy the various heated rooms, cold pools, and communal relaxation areas. Many jjimjilbangs are open 24 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel, check out, and do any final souvenir shopping in the Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center. Head to Incheon Airport via AREX or limousine bus. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for check-in and security at Incheon International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Enjoy a final Korean meal at one of the airport's many restaurants before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (last one!) or a local bakery near the hotel
meals.lunch: Bupyeong area — a quick and satisfying bowl of Sundubu Jjigae (순두부찌개, soft tofu stew) or Kimchi Jjigae at a local restaurant (₩8,000–₩12,000)
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport — try a proper sit-down Korean meal at one of the airport restaurants. Bibimbap or Doenjang Jjigae set meal is a classic final Korean meal (₩12,000–₩18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at Toyoko Inn is typically 11:00 AM. Incheon Airport is one of the world's best airports — arrive early and enjoy the duty-free shopping, cultural performances, and excellent facilities. The AREX train from Bupyeong to Incheon Airport takes approximately 40–50 minutes. Don't forget to get a VAT refund on eligible purchases before departing!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the iconic 14th-century Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok robe. Many rental shops surrounding the palace offer affordable Hanbok rentals, and wearing one grants you free entry to the palace. Witness the ceremonial Changing of the Royal Guard and stroll through the grand courtyards for an immersive dive into Joseon Dynasty culture.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional market, famous for its vibrant food stalls. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (mini seaweed rice rolls), tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the authentic sights, sounds, and flavors of everyday Korean culinary life.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Dance Class
experiences.description: Learn choreography from your favorite K-Pop songs at one of Hongdae's many dedicated K-Pop dance academies. Professional instructors teach routines from groups like BTS, BLACKPINK, and NewJeans in a fun, energetic group setting. This is a quintessential K-culture experience that lets you live out your idol fantasies and connect with fellow K-Pop fans from around the world.

experiences.name: Insadong Cultural Village & Tea House Exploration
experiences.description: Wander through the charming alleyways of Insadong, Seoul's premier cultural district filled with traditional tea houses, antique shops, indie galleries, and Korean craft stores. Stop into a traditional Hanok-style tea house to enjoy a ceremonial cup of omija (five-flavor berry) or barley tea paired with Korean rice cakes. Explore Ssamziegil, a quirky open-air shopping complex showcasing local artisan goods and handmade crafts.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 22:30 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight is late evening
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange private airport transfer to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Check in, freshen up, and settle into the hotel. Light late-night snack near the hotel if hungry.

meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store snack or 24-hour ramen shop near Bupyeong station (Bupyeong is known for its night food scene)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night — prioritize rest. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance. Keep luggage light for easy transit. Exchange some KRW at the airport for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely hotel breakfast, then explore Bupyeong Modoo Mall and the underground shopping arcade — one of Korea's largest underground markets, great for getting a feel for local life. Browse boutiques and warm up with a hot coffee at a local café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Incheon Chinatown and Jayu Park — a short taxi or subway ride away. Explore the colorful murals, traditional Chinese architecture, and the historic Jayu Park offering panoramic views of Incheon port. Visit the nearby Sinpo International Market for local Incheon snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong area for a premium Korean BBQ dinner at a top-rated local galbi restaurant. Enjoy premium Hanwoo beef with banchan side dishes and traditional Korean rice wine (makgeolli).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café with Korean-style toast and coffee
meals.lunch: Sinpo International Market — try Sinpo-style fried chicken (the original!) and hotteok sweet pancakes
meals.dinner: Premium Hanwoo Korean BBQ restaurant in Bupyeong — budget ₩80,000–120,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is an orientation day to recover from jet lag while exploring the local Incheon area. Dress warmly — temperatures around 3°C. Layering is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway or private car into central Seoul (approx. 40–50 min from Bupyeong). Begin the day at Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience — arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat crowds. Rent a stunning traditional Hanbok robe from a premium rental shop near the palace gates and explore the iconic 14th-century palace grounds, including Geunjeongjeon throne hall and the scenic Hyangwonjeong pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village — a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll the winding alleys, admire the architecture, and stop into a premium craft gallery or traditional pottery studio. Visit Changdeokgung Palace's Secret Garden (Huwon) if time permits — a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong Cultural Village for an early evening exploration of its charming alleyways, traditional tea houses, and artisan shops. Enjoy a premium multi-course Korean dinner at a renowned Insadong restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing for Seoul
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean set meal (hanjeongsik) near Gyeongbokgung — try a restaurant offering royal court cuisine
meals.dinner: Premium Korean fine dining in Insadong — try Sanchon (temple food) or a high-end Korean restaurant offering seasonal tasting menus, ₩100,000+ per person

day_by_day.notes: Hanbok rental typically costs ₩20,000–40,000 for 2–3 hours. Wearing Hanbok grants free entry to Gyeongbokgung Palace. Book Changdeokgung Secret Garden tour in advance — limited daily visitors. Dress in warm layers under the Hanbok.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Insadong Cultural Village & Tea House Exploration in depth — spend the morning wandering through Ssamziegil courtyard, browsing independent galleries, calligraphy shops, and traditional craft stores. Settle into a premium traditional tea house for a ceremonial tea experience with Korean rice cakes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore nearby Jogyesa Temple — Seoul's most important Buddhist temple, beautifully decorated with lanterns in winter. Then head to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a peaceful winter walk along the illuminated urban waterway, admiring the seasonal light installations.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Myeongdong for a premium skincare and cosmetics shopping experience — visit flagship stores of Sulwhasoo, History of Whoo, and other luxury Korean beauty brands. Enjoy a premium dinner in the area.

meals.lunch: Upscale café lunch in Insadong — try a traditional Korean bento-style dosirak set
meals.dinner: Premium Japanese-Korean fusion or upscale Korean restaurant in Myeongdong — try Myeongdong Kyoja for their legendary kalguksu noodles (iconic, not expensive but authentic) or a nearby premium restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Insadong is best explored on foot. Cheonggyecheon Stream is especially beautiful in winter evenings with light festivals. Myeongdong can be crowded on Friday evenings — go early for shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour — arrive at Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional market (open since 1905) for an immersive morning food tour. Sample bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), yukhoe (Korean beef tartare), and freshly made tteok rice cakes. Engage with the passionate market vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's futuristic landmark. Browse design exhibitions, pop-up stores, and the surrounding Dongdaemun fashion district. Visit the Dongdaemun History & Culture Park for a blend of ancient and modern Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam district for a premium evening. Visit the upscale COEX Mall and Starfield Library, then enjoy a world-class dinner at one of Gangnam's Michelin-starred or highly acclaimed restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast before the food tour
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market food tour IS the lunch — budget ₩30,000–50,000 for a full tasting spread
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred Korean restaurant in Gangnam — consider Gaon (3 Michelin stars, royal Korean cuisine) or Jungsik for modern Korean, ₩200,000–300,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is busiest on Saturdays — arrive by 10:00 AM for the best experience. Book Michelin-starred dinner well in advance. Gangnam is about 30 min from Gwangjang by subway.

day_by_day.morning: Visit N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) — take the cable car up Namsan Mountain for panoramic winter views of Seoul. Attach a love lock on the famous fence, explore the observation deck, and enjoy the crisp winter air. The city looks spectacular in clear winter weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon and Haebangchon (HBC) — Seoul's most cosmopolitan neighborhood. Browse luxury antique shops, international boutiques, and the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Korea's finest private art museums featuring both Korean traditional art and contemporary international works.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium international dining experience in Itaewon — the neighborhood is home to some of Seoul's best fine dining restaurants. Alternatively, explore the vibrant Itaewon nightlife scene with craft cocktails at a rooftop bar.

meals.lunch: Upscale café or restaurant near Namsan — try a premium Korean brunch spot
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Itaewon — consider Dore Dore for creative Korean desserts and dinner, or Vatos Urban Tacos for a fun Korean-Mexican fusion, or a high-end steakhouse

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower cable car operates from 10:00 AM. Leeum Museum is closed on Mondays — Sunday is perfect. Dress very warmly for Namsan — wind chill makes it feel significantly colder than 3°C.

day_by_day.morning: K-Pop Idol Dance Class in Hongdae — head to Seoul's vibrant youth and arts district for a 2-hour K-Pop dance class at one of Hongdae's dedicated academies (like Def Dance Skool or K-Arts Academy). Learn choreography from iconic K-Pop songs with a professional instructor. A truly immersive K-culture experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hongdae's street art, indie boutiques, and K-Pop merchandise stores. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or LINE Friends flagship store. Browse vinyl record shops and independent fashion boutiques that define Hongdae's creative culture.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for dinner and evening entertainment. Experience the famous Hongdae street performances (busking culture), then enjoy craft cocktails and Korean fried chicken at a premium pojangmacha-style venue or rooftop bar.

meals.lunch: Trendy Hongdae café lunch — try a popular brunch spot like Café Bora (known for purple taro lattes) or a premium Korean fusion café
meals.dinner: Premium Korean fried chicken and craft beer pairing at a top Hongdae restaurant, or upscale Korean BBQ in the area

day_by_day.notes: Book the K-Pop dance class at least 3–5 days in advance. Classes typically cost ₩30,000–60,000 per person. Wear comfortable clothes for dancing. Hongdae is most lively in the evening — great for people-watching.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site just 30 minutes from Seoul by KTX or subway. Walk the impressive 5.7km fortress walls, visit the Hwaseong Haenggung Palace, and explore the traditional Suwon Hwaseong Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Suwon's traditional culture at the Korean Folk Village (Minsokchon) — a living museum showcasing traditional Korean architecture, crafts, and performances. Watch traditional folk performances and artisan demonstrations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and head to the upscale Cheongdam-dong area in Gangnam — Seoul's answer to Beverly Hills. Browse luxury flagship stores (Chanel, Dior, Louis Vuitton Korean flagship), then enjoy a premium dinner at a celebrity-chef restaurant.

meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (short rib BBQ) — Suwon is nationally famous for this dish. Try a traditional restaurant near the fortress
meals.dinner: Upscale restaurant in Cheongdam-dong — try Mingles (Michelin-starred modern Korean) or a premium omakase experience, ₩150,000–250,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is about 30 min from Seoul Station by subway (Line 1). The fortress walls can be icy in December — wear sturdy shoes. Korean Folk Village is about 20 min from the fortress by taxi.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and arguably Seoul's most beautiful palace. Take the guided English tour of the Secret Garden (Huwon), a stunning royal garden with ancient trees, pavilions, and lotus ponds. The winter atmosphere is serene and magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a quieter, more authentic alternative to Bukchon. Wander through traditional alleyways, visit independent art galleries, and discover hidden cafés in converted hanok houses. Visit the Gyeonghuigung Palace ruins nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Korean performance — book tickets for a Nanta show (dynamic non-verbal cooking performance), a traditional gugak music concert at the National Theater of Korea, or a B-Boy performance. Follow with a premium dinner.

meals.lunch: Premium hanok café lunch in Seochon — try a traditional Korean set meal in a beautifully restored hanok house
meals.dinner: Pre-theater or post-theater dinner near Namsan or central Seoul — try a premium Korean restaurant specializing in seasonal winter ingredients like kimchi jjigae with premium pork belly

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours must be booked in advance at the palace website. Tours run at specific times and are limited to small groups. The National Theater of Korea is near Namsan — check performance schedules in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea — one of Asia's largest military museums, offering profound insight into Korean history, the Korean War, and the nation's resilience. The outdoor exhibits include tanks, aircraft, and naval vessels. A deeply moving cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Lotte World Tower and Lotte World Mall in Jamsil — visit the Sky Observatory on the 117th–123rd floors for breathtaking panoramic views of Seoul. Browse the luxury retail floors and explore the adjacent Lotte World theme park or Seokchon Lake.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve special experience — Seoul transforms beautifully for Christmas. Enjoy the festive lights at Cheonggyecheon Stream or Gwanghwamun Square, then celebrate with a premium Christmas Eve dinner at a top Seoul hotel restaurant or fine dining establishment.

meals.lunch: Upscale restaurant in the Yongsan/Itaewon area near the War Memorial
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner — consider the Grand Hyatt Seoul, Signiel Seoul (in Lotte World Tower), or a premium French-Korean fusion restaurant. Reserve well in advance, ₩200,000–400,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is a major celebration in Seoul — restaurants will be fully booked. Reserve dinner at least 2 weeks in advance. Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory tickets can be purchased online. The city will be beautifully decorated.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed Christmas morning — enjoy a luxurious hotel breakfast or brunch. Then visit Gyeongbokgung Palace again for the Changing of the Royal Guard ceremony (held at 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM) — a spectacular traditional performance in full Joseon Dynasty military regalia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of the world's largest museums, housing over 220,000 artifacts spanning Korean history from prehistoric times to the Joseon Dynasty. The museum is free and world-class. Spend 2–3 hours exploring highlights.
day_by_day.evening: Premium Christmas dinner and K-culture evening — enjoy a festive Korean-style Christmas dinner, then explore the Gangnam or Hongdae nightlife scene. Many venues host special Christmas events with live music and performances.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious hotel brunch — treat yourself to a premium spread
meals.lunch: Museum café or nearby upscale restaurant in Yongsan
meals.dinner: Premium Korean Christmas dinner — try a high-end Korean restaurant offering a special holiday menu, or a luxury hotel buffet with Korean and international options

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea — most attractions remain open. The National Museum of Korea is free entry. Book Christmas dinner in advance. The Changing of the Guard is a must-see cultural spectacle.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namdaemun Market — Seoul's largest traditional market, open since 1414. Explore the labyrinthine stalls selling everything from Korean street food to textiles, kitchenware, and ginseng. A fascinating contrast to the modern city. Try freshly made hotteok and galguksu noodles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Han River (Hangang) — rent a bicycle or take a leisurely walk along the riverside parks. Visit Yeouido Hangang Park for winter views of the river. Then explore the IFC Seoul Mall in Yeouido for premium shopping and a coffee break.
day_by_day.evening: Final premium K-culture evening — visit a luxury jjimjilbang (Korean spa) for a traditional Korean sauna and body scrub experience (Italy towel exfoliation). This is an essential Korean wellness ritual. Follow with a farewell premium Korean dinner.

meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market food experience — try kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup), hotteok, and various street snacks
meals.dinner: Premium farewell Korean dinner — try a top-rated samgyeopsal (pork belly BBQ) restaurant or a high-end Korean seafood restaurant. Consider Noryangjin Fish Market for a premium live seafood experience — choose your fish and have it prepared upstairs

day_by_day.notes: Namdaemun Market is busiest on Saturday mornings — arrive early. For the jjimjilbang, Dragon Hill Spa in Yongsan is the most famous luxury option (open 24 hours). Noryangjin Fish Market is open early morning — best for lunch rather than dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Take a short walk around Bupyeong for last-minute shopping at the underground arcade or pick up Korean snacks, cosmetics, and souvenirs. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and arrange private transfer to Incheon International Airport (approximately 20–30 minutes from Bupyeong). Arrive at the airport with ample time — at least 3 hours before international departure. Explore the world-class Incheon Airport duty-free shops for last-minute luxury Korean purchases (cosmetics, ginseng, Korean spirits, designer goods).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Enjoy a final Korean meal at one of the premium airport restaurants before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy Korean-style breakfast with doenjang jjigae (soybean paste soup), rice, and banchan
meals.lunch: Premium airport restaurant — Incheon Airport has excellent dining options including Korean BBQ, bibimbap, and international cuisine
meals.dinner: On the flight or at the airport departure lounge

day_by_day.notes: Incheon Airport duty-free is exceptional — budget extra time for shopping. Consider purchasing: Sulwhasoo or History of Whoo luxury skincare sets, Korean red ginseng products, Jeju tangerine chocolates, and premium Korean teas. Keep receipts for tax refund claims. Confirm flight details and transfer timing the night before.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX
